title: The read-only check and the executed statement are the same text: CR-ended comments, JDBC escapes and SHOW/DESC shortcut cannot smuggle a second statement or a denied function

criteria.given: a logged-in ROLE_SQL_EXEC caller posting SELECT 1 AS a --<CR>, 2 AS b (a line comment H2/PostgreSQL end at CR, so the executed statement has two columns)
criteria.then: the workbench refuses it with 400 READ_ONLY_VIOLATION — the statement that is validated is the statement that would be executed

criteria.given: the same caller posting a JDBC function escape that a deny-listed function hides inside (SELECT CAST({fn FILE_READ('/tmp/canary.txt', NULL)} AS VARCHAR) AS c)
criteria.then: the workbench refuses it with 400 READ_ONLY_VIOLATION — JDBC escapes never reach the driver

criteria.given: the same caller posting a statement starting with SHOW that carries stacked DDL behind a CR-ended comment (SHOW TABLES --<CR>; CREATE LOCAL TEMPORARY TABLE T3(X INT); DROP TABLE T3)
criteria.then: the workbench refuses it with 400 READ_ONLY_VIOLATION — a SHOW/DESC/DESCRIBE statement cannot carry a second statement

criteria.given: the same caller posting an ordinary read-only SELECT 1
criteria.then: the workbench still answers 200 with the row — the guard did not narrow what a legitimate analyst runs

steps.name: a CR-terminated line comment hiding extra columns is rejected with READ_ONLY_VIOLATION
a JDBC function escape hiding a deny-listed function is rejected with READ_ONLY_VIOLATION
a SHOW statement stacking DDL behind a CR-ended comment is rejected with READ_ONLY_VIOLATION
